title: When Does Grokking Change the Circuit? Tracking Circuit Identity Through Phase Transitions

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible link to safety: if circuits reorganize at phase transitions, training-time interpretability snapshots may not represent deployed behavior. But the connection from toy grokking tasks to real-world safety is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training transformers from scratch, running automated circuit discovery (edge attribution patching) at many checkpoints, and understanding phase transition dynamics. Advanced for beginners even with TransformerLens.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Many training checkpoints each requiring circuit discovery analysis creates sustained effort. The analysis pipeline is non-trivial. Partially achievable in 30 hours but comprehensive results would need more time.

novelty.reasoning: Grokking and its phase transitions have been extensively studied mechanistically since Nanda et al. (2023). The construct-then-compress dynamics and circuit formation during grokking are documented. However, the specific question of tracking full circuit identity (not just progress measures) through the transition, and systematically mapping how circuit topology changes at each phase, has not been comprehensively addressed. The incremental contribution would be in the circuit-tracking methodology rather than the core phenomenon.

evidence.source: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability (Neel Nanda et al., 2023)
evidence.finding: Seminal work using mechanistic interpretability to track progress measures through grokking, showing the formation of Fourier-based feature maps and trigonometric circuits during the phase transition.

evidence.source: Grokking as a First Order Phase Transition (ICLR 2024)
evidence.finding: Characterizes grokking as a first-order phase transition with information-theoretic measures, showing synergy spikes at transition points.
Recent work on the geometric and architectural topology aspects of grokking phase transitions, showing construct-then-compress dynamics.
